title: policy rule
description: A single ABAC rule within a Policy. Referenced by policy create/update request schemas and policy get/list/create/update response schemas.

id.description: Stable client-assigned rule identifier (scoped to the policy).

effect.$comment: enum: allow, deny — minLength/maxLength guards are length-based equivalents; add enum: [allow, deny] here if a future schema upgrade can break existing clients
effect.description: Authorization verdict. Valid values: allow, deny. Deny-overrides: any deny wins over all allows.

action.$comment: Action target set (#1979). Non-empty restricts the rule to requests whose action (permission name, e.g. audit:read) is in the set; empty/absent = untargeted. REQUIRED non-empty for allow rules — enforced at the domain layer (abac.Rule.Validate → 422), not structurally, keeping the domain validator the single source of structural truth (per #1977 convention). Empty/absent stays valid for deny rules (deny-all).
action.description: Permission names this rule targets (e.g. ["audit:read"]). MUST be non-empty for allow rules: an allow rule must name which route gate(s) it widens, otherwise one blank allow could blow open the route gate for every permission. Empty or absent is allowed only for deny rules (deny-all).

conditions.description: All conditions are AND-combined. Empty or absent means unconditional (rule always applies).

source.$comment: enum: subject, resource, environment — minLength/maxLength guards are length-based equivalents
source.description: Attribute namespace. Valid values: subject (principal claims), resource (protected object attrs), environment (context).

key.description: Attribute name within the source namespace (e.g. department, classification, time_of_day).

operator.$comment: enum: eq, neq, in, not_in, eq_attr — minLength/maxLength guards are length-based equivalents; maxLength bumped to 7 to admit eq_attr (7 chars)
operator.description: Comparison applied between the resolved attribute and the right-hand side. Valid values: eq, neq, in, not_in (static: compare against values), eq_attr (cross-attribute: compare against rhsSource/rhsKey instead of values).

values.description: Right-hand side of the comparison for static operators (eq, neq, in, not_in). Must be non-empty when present. Absent for cross-attribute operator eq_attr.

rhsSource.$comment: enum: subject, resource, environment — same shape as source; only valid when operator is eq_attr
rhsSource.description: Cross-attribute right-hand-side namespace. Set only for operator eq_attr. Valid values: subject, resource, environment.

rhsKey.description: Cross-attribute right-hand-side attribute name. Set only for operator eq_attr.

items.$comment: Operator-discriminated RHS shape (#1977): static operators (eq/neq/in/not_in) carry a non-empty `values` and no RHS reference; the cross-attribute operator eq_attr carries `rhsSource`+`rhsKey` and no `values`. Enforced structurally so a malformed mix is rejected at the schema layer (400), preserving the pre-eq_attr 400 status for static conditions missing `values` (which would otherwise fall through to the domain validator's 422).

obligations.description: Obligations imposed on the PEP when this rule matches. All fields are optional.

rowScope.$comment: enum: self, device, tenant (all is wire-valid vocabulary but rejected by policy authoring — see description); minLength/maxLength guards are length-based equivalents and intentionally still admit 'all' so the server rejects it semantically (422), not structurally (400)
rowScope.description: Row-visibility obligation. Grantable values: self, device, tenant. The value 'all' (cross-tenant) is reserved for the audited super-admin derivation and is rejected with 422 when supplied via policy authoring. Absent means no row-scope constraint.

fieldMask.description: Fields the PEP must redact from the response. Absent or empty means no field-mask obligation.
